title: Russian Missile Strike Kills 5 Kametstal Workers in Kamianske, Hours Into US Peace Push
detail: Russian forces struck the Kametstal metallurgical plant in Kamianske, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, with ballistic missiles in the early hours of September 5, killing five plant employees and injuring five others; one additional worker was reported missing, with only his backpack found at the scene. Governor Oleksandr Hanzha said three of the injured were hospitalized, including a 30-year-old woman in intensive care. Kametstal, one of Ukraine's largest steelmakers and one of the few major industrial plants to keep operating through the war, halted operations after the strike. The attack came hours after Ukraine had ordered its own troops to observe a temporary halt on long-range strikes on Moscow and Kyiv to enable US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to travel for peace talks, underscoring that front-line and rear-area strikes continued despite the capital-focused pause.

title: Witkoff and Kushner Hold Three-Hour Kremlin Meeting With Putin as Capitals Truce Takes Effect
detail: US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin for a three-hour session on September 5, followed by dinner, reviving direct US-Russia peace contacts after months of stalled diplomacy. Putin's foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov called the talks 'constructive' though no breakthrough was announced. Putin ordered a 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv timed to the envoys' visit, and Ukraine reciprocated by pausing long-range strikes on Moscow, to allow the delegation's onward overland travel to Kyiv on September 6. Witkoff and Kushner described discussing 'substantive plans for next steps' toward ending the war.

title: IAEA Brokers Seventh Localized Ceasefire to Repair Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant's Last Power Line
detail: A localized ceasefire brokered by the IAEA took effect on September 5 near the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, allowing Ukrainian technicians to repair the 330-kilovolt Ferosplavna-1 line — the plant's sole remaining external power connection, severed since August 20 by fighting north of the Dnipro River. The plant had been relying on emergency diesel generators to cool its six reactors and spent fuel pools and was running low on fuel, raising the risk of a station blackout. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said an agency team would monitor the repair work, which followed demining of the area; it was the seventh such localized truce negotiated at the plant since the war began.
